topic: Two siblings inherit their grandmother's house
text:
Two siblings stroll into my office, fancy clothes, fresh off the street, all smiles. They got themselves a grandma who just up and left them a house. Like it’s some kind of fairy tale. "We need your help sorting out a mess," the brother says, all smooth and polished. His sister nods, all eyes and fake sympathy. Mess? More like a web of lies, I bet. Houses don’t just get passed down clean. Some sweat, some blood—usually more than a little. I lean back, hands behind my head. "Grandma didn’t tell you everything, did she?" I ask, already knowing the answer. They shift, uncomfortable, the smiles slipping.
